stem: The rate of chemical reactions is affected by changes in temperature and pressure.

parts.label: (a)(i)
(a)(ii)
parts.text:
On the diagram in (a)(i), draw a second curve to show the distribution of energies of the krypton atoms at a higher temperature.

Label the second curve $\mathbf{T2}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The Boltzmann distribution assumes that the particles behave as an ideal gas.
parts.text: State **two** assumptions of the kinetic theory as applied to an ideal gas.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
$2.00\text{ g}$ of krypton gas, $\text{Kr(g)}$, is placed in a sealed $5.00\text{ dm}^3$ container at $120^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Calculate the pressure, in Pa, of $\text{Kr(g)}$ in the container. Assume $\text{Kr(g)}$ behaves as an ideal gas.

Show your working.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State and explain the conditions at which krypton behaves most like an ideal gas.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
Krypton reacts with fluorine in the presence of ultraviolet light to make krypton difluoride, $\text{KrF}_2\text{(g)}$.

$$\text{Kr(g)} + \text{F}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{KrF}_2\text{(g)}$$

activation energy for the reaction, $E_{\text{a}} = +385\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

enthalpy change of formation of $\text{KrF}_2$, $\Delta H_{\text{f}} = +60.2\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain, in terms of activation energy, $E_{\text{a}}$, and the collision of particles, how an increase in temperature affects the rate of a chemical reaction.
